office: Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH)
subject: Warning Letter — Quality System Regulation violations, class II devices
content:
[SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE — fictional letter written for the WarnSync reference implementation. Not a real FDA record.]

Dear Mr. Okonkwo:

During an inspection of your medical device manufacturing facility conducted from March 31 to April 11, 2025, an investigator from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration determined that your firm manufactures powered infusion pumps. These products are devices under section 201(h) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. This inspection revealed that these devices are adulterated because the methods used in, or the facilities or controls used for, their manufacture, packing, storage, or installation are not in conformity with the Quality System regulation, 21 CFR part 820.

1. Failure to establish and maintain procedures for implementing corrective and preventive action (21 CFR 820.100(a)). Your CAPA procedure QP-800 does not require analysis of quality data sources to identify existing and potential causes of nonconforming product. Of the nineteen CAPAs opened in 2024, twelve were closed without verification that the corrective action was effective and did not adversely affect the finished device.

2. Failure to establish and maintain procedures for receiving, reviewing, and evaluating complaints (21 CFR 820.198(a)). Your firm received 214 complaints in 2024 describing unintended free flow of infusate. Your complaint handling unit classified 186 of these as "user error" without device evaluation. No determination was made as to whether the events were reportable under 21 CFR part 803.

3. Failure to validate a process whose results cannot be fully verified by subsequent inspection and test (21 CFR 820.75(a)). The ultrasonic welding process used to seal your pump cassette was revalidated in 2021; your firm subsequently changed the cassette resin supplier in 2023 without revalidation and without a documented change assessment.

4. Failure to establish and maintain procedures to ensure that the device design is correctly translated into production specifications (21 CFR 820.30(h)). The design output for the occlusion alarm threshold was recorded in the design history file as a range, while the production specification carried a single nominal value with no tolerance.

Your response should address the systemic nature of these deficiencies, not only the specific examples cited.

5. Failure to establish and maintain procedures for changes to a specification, method, process, or procedure (21 CFR 820.70(b)). Seven engineering changes implemented on the cassette assembly line during 2024 were documented on the production floor by a manufacturing engineer and were not routed to the change control board.

6. Failure to establish and maintain procedures to control product that does not conform to specified requirements (21 CFR 820.90(a)). Nonconforming pump housings were segregated in an area labeled "hold" that was not physically restricted, and 340 units were drawn from that area into production during the inspection period.

Medical Device Reporting. Our review of your complaint files identified events that appear to meet the reporting criteria of 21 CFR part 803. Free-flow events of the type described in your complaint records may have caused or contributed to a serious injury. Your firm's failure to evaluate these complaints for reportability is a violation of 21 CFR 803.50(a). You should review all complaints received since January 2023 against your reporting procedure and submit any required reports.

Conclusion. The violations described above are not intended to be an all-inclusive list. You are responsible for investigating and determining the causes of any violations and for preventing their recurrence or the occurrence of other violations. Federal agencies are advised of the issuance of all warning letters about devices so that they may take this information into account when considering the award of contracts.
